न गोली न बम…हैकर्स ने फ्रिज का तापमान 50 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक बढ़ाकर सड़ा दिया खाना; फ्रांस में अजीबोगरीब साइबर अटैक
फ्रांस के सैकड़ों सुपरमार्केट में 11-12 अक्टूबर की रात को हैकरों ने फ्रीजर को हीटर में बदल दिया। दूर बैठकर उन्होंने रेफ्रिजरेशन सिस्टम को गर्म कर दिया, जिससे तापमान 50 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक पहुंच गया। आइसक्रीम पिघल गई, खाना खराब हो गया और कुछ जगहों पर आग लगने की खबरें हैं।
फ्रांस से हैरान करने वाली एक खबर सामने आई है। यहां के सैकड़ों सुपरमार्केट में 11 और 12 अक्टूबर की रात को एक बड़ा साइबर अटैक हुआ। हैकरों ने दूर से रेफ्रिजरेशन सिस्टम को नियंत्रित करके फ्रीजर को हीटर जैसा बना दिया। मशीनें चल रही थीं, लेकिन वे अब स्टोर मालिकों के आदेश नहीं मान रही थीं। तापमान तेजी से बढ़ा और कई जगह 50 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक पहुंच गया। यह वही गर्मी है जो दिल्ली में मई के महीने में पड़ती है। बाद सुपरमार्केट मैनेजरों ने देखा कि आइसक्रीम और दूसरे जमे हुए खाने पिघलने लगे। खाना खराब हो गया। कुछ स्टोर में आग लगने की खबरें भी आईं। हमला इतना तेज और व्यापक था कि कई सुपरमार्केट एक साथ प्रभावित हुए।
बता दें कि फ्रीजर का काम खाना ठंडा रखना होता है। लेकिन उस रात मशीनें चलते हुए भी तापमान बढ़ा रही थीं। कंट्रोलर हर कमांड मान रहा था, बस वह कमांड स्टोर के मैनेजर का नहीं, बल्कि हैकरों का था। हैकर दूर बैठकर सिस्टम को गर्म कर रहे थे।
एक साल पहले बता दी गई थी कमजोरी
इंडिया टुडे से बात करते हुए इजरायली साइबर सिक्योरिटी कंपनी क्लारोटी के CTO और टीम82 के हेड आमिर प्रेमिंगर ने बताया कि उन्होंने एक साल से भी ज्यादा पहले डैनफॉस कंपनी को इस कमजोरी के बारे में सूचना दी थी। इस कमजोरी से हमलावर बिना सही पासवर्ड के सिस्टम में घुस सकता था। डैनफॉस ने इस कमजोरी को ठीक करके सॉफ्टवेयर अपडेट जारी कर दिया था। लेकिन फिक्स निकलने के बावजूद समस्या खत्म नहीं हुई। प्रेमिंगर ने कहा कि इसके बावजूद इंटरनेट पर जो बहुत सारे डिवाइस हम देखते हैं, वे उस समय भी कमजोर थे।
डैनफॉस की एडवाइजरी में क्या चेतावनी?
डैनफॉस की अपनी एडवाइजरी में साफ लिखा था कि उनके रेफ्रिजरेशन कंट्रोलर में एक सुरक्षा कमी है। इस कमी से हमलावर पासवर्ड प्रोटेक्शन को बायपास कर सकते हैं। इस कमजोरी को 10 में से 8.2 रेटिंग दी गई थी। एडवाइजरी में यह भी चेतावनी दी गई थी कि हमलावर इंटरनल आईपी एड्रेस, यूजरनेम और स्टोर का नाम जैसी जानकारी भी देख सकते हैं। ये कंट्रोलर ऑपरेटर को दूर से ही तापमान और शेड्यूल बदलने की सुविधा देते हैं। अगर हमलावर को एक्सेस मिल जाए तो वे आसानी से खाने को ठंडा रखने वाले सिस्टम को गर्म कर सकते हैं।
कितने डिवाइस खुले?
क्लारोटी को अपने पुराने स्कैन में 2765 डैनफॉस कंट्रोलर ऑनलाइन मिले थे। बाद में रॉयटर्स को शोडान पर कम से कम 4500 डैनफॉस इंटरफेस दिखे। ये अलग-अलग स्कैन हैं। ये संख्या बताती है कि कितने डिवाइस इंटरनेट पर खुले थे, न कि कितने हैक हो चुके थे। प्रेमिंगर ने समझाया कि सेन्सिस और शोडान सिर्फ स्कैन करके रिपोर्ट करते हैं। वे बता सकते हैं कि कौन सा कंट्रोलर ऑनलाइन है, लेकिन यह कन्फर्म नहीं कर सकते कि वह कमजोर है या नहीं। फिर भी, जितने ज्यादा डिवाइस इंटरनेट पर खुले रहेंगे, हमलावरों को उतने ही ज्यादा रास्ते मिल सकते हैं। फ्रांसीसी स्कैनिंग फर्म ओनीफे ने रॉयटर्स को बताया कि उन्होंने जिन इंटरफेस की जांच की, उनमें से सिर्फ कुछ ही लेटेस्ट सॉफ्टवेयर चला रहे थे।
हैकर्स ने कैसे किया अटैक?
प्रेमिंगर ने साफ कहा कि हमारे पास इस बारे में कोई तथ्य नहीं है कि हमलावर कैसे अंदर आए और वास्तव में डीफ्रॉस्ट प्रक्रिया शुरू करने में सक्षम थे। उन्होंने दो संभावनाएं बताईं, दोनों की अभी पुष्टि नहीं हुई है। पहली संभावना है कि डिवाइस पर डिफॉल्ट पासवर्ड लगा था, जिसे हैकरों ने क्रैक किया या कहीं से लीक हो गया। दूसरी संभावना है कि क्लारोटी ने जो कमजोरी बताई थी, हैकरों ने उसे फिर से बना लिया। क्योंकि पूरी टेक्निकल डिटेल्स कभी पब्लिक नहीं की गई थीं। प्रेमिंगर ने क्लारोटी के एक ब्लॉग पोस्ट का भी जिक्र किया जिसमें दावा किया गया था कि AI लगभग 6 डॉलर में 28 मिनट में उस कमजोरी का पता लगा सकता है।
सिर्फ रेफ्रिजरेशन तक नहीं
बताया जा रहा है कि यह खतरा सिर्फ सुपरमार्केट तक सीमित नहीं। जुलाई 2026 में अमेरिका में कम से कम सात राज्यों की पानी और वेस्टवॉटर यूटिलिटी पर भी ऐसे हमले हुए थे। हमलावरों ने सेटिंग्स और पासवर्ड बदल दिए थे, जिससे पानी का प्रेशर गिरा और बाढ़ आई। फ्रांसीसी CERT ने अलर्ट जारी किया है कि हमले अभी भी जारी हो सकते हैं। इसमें डैनफॉस, कोपलैंड और डिक्सेल के कंट्रोलर शामिल हैं। सिर्फ फैक्टरी रीसेट काफी नहीं है। डिवाइस फिर से हैक हो सकता है।

MUMBAI: The city was under a heatwave warning for the third consecutive day on Wednesday with a yellow alert issued by the
IMD.
For Oct 14, the weather bureau has warned of hot and humid weather conditions in isolated areas as temperatures continue to remain elevated.
Maximum temperature recorded on Wednesday by the IMD Santacruz observatory was 37.8 deg C, which was 4.1 deg C above normal, while the IMD Colaba observatory recorded 36.4 deg C, which was 3.2 deg C above normal.
Mumbai has been placed under a heatwave warning for Oct 15, with Oct 16 forecast to witness hot and humid weather conditions. Meanwhile, light to moderate rain and thundershowers are expected for Oct 17-18 for Mumbai and Thane.
Just a day ago, the city had recorded a maximum temperature of 38°C, making it the second-hottest Oct day in 11 years. Meanwhile, mercury had touched 38.2°C on Monday, the highest Oct maximum recorded in the city during the same period.
IMD officials too agreed that a prolonged heatwave for early in the month of Oct wasn’t very common.
“The anticyclone which led to the first heatwave warning on Oct 9 last week has shifted slightly northwards, but an easterly wave is influencing the region, with temperatures likely to touch 37.8°C on Thursday.
This will mean seven consecutive days of temperatures above 37°C, which is unusually oppressive for Mumbai. While the city does experience spells of two to three days of high temperatures, a continuous stretch of six to seven days is not normal. An easterly wave is a weather system characterised by a trough that travels from east to west. It is a feature of this season and can interact with weather systems approaching from the west, triggering intense thunderstorms. Its role in prolonging the current hot spell is a factor that needs to be examined, particularly in the context of a strong El Niño year,” said an IMD official.
According to Akshay Sunil, Vice President, WeatherEx Pvt Ltd, “The heat over Mumbai is part of a broader warm spell across western India. A high-pressure circulation and easterly to northeasterly winds are limiting the usual cooling sea breeze, while clear post-monsoon skies are allowing strong daytime heating. Humidity adds to the discomfort. Our extended outlook suggests that above-normal temperatures may continue through at least October 22, although local light showers could bring temporary relief post Oct 22 in parts of Konkan.”

Zermatt Reopens for Glacier Skiing After Three-Month Heatwave Shutdown (1)
14/October/2026
Skiers and snowboarders return to the Theodul glacier today, 14 October, when Zermatt reopens its high-altitude slopes. The Swiss resort’s glacier area normally runs all year, but it has been closed since the end of July, when a summer heatwave left conditions unsafe. Fresh snow and cooler temperatures now allow a limited restart.
Back on the Theodul glacier
Zermatt/Cervinia aims to stay open all year, but it was forced to close on 31 July and has stayed shut ever since. The suspension followed exceptionally high temperatures and a lack of snowfall that left the pistes unsuitable for safe skiing. It also affected Cervinia, on the Italian side, which sells access to the same cross-border summer product.
The reopening is deliberately modest. From today the Plateau Rosa 1 and 2 ski lifts are available to guests, and the Matterhorn Glacier Ride II between Klein Matterhorn and Testa Grigia also resumes. Preparations are under way to open Plateau Rosa 3, which, subject to conditions, would add a beginners’ area and a small selection of snowpark features. The lift company stressed that the extent of the skiing on offer will depend on snow, weather and operating conditions. The restart is a continuation of summer skiing rather than a full opening of the resort, which is slated for 1 November.
The operator, Zermatt Bergbahnen, credited the reopening to preparation and maintenance work by its staff. Live lift and slope information is published at matterhornparadise.ch/timetable.
A rare interruption for the Alps’ highest ski area
Until this summer Zermatt was a 365-day-a-year ski resort. Its glacier ski area reaches nearly 4,000 metres, the highest in the Alps, and is normally one of the most snow-sure places on Earth. The area has been interrupted before. Glacier skiing was also halted during the exceptionally hot summer of 2022.
Zermatt now joins a small group of glacier areas offering snow. PlanetSKI counts eight already open: Hintertux, Pitztal, Sölden, Stubai and Kitzsteinhorn in Austria, Saas-Fee in Switzerland, and Val Senales and Passo Stelvio in Italy. Zermatt makes nine. The forecast offers little help for the days ahead. The weather this week is expected to be more settled with rising temperatures, and no significant snow is forecast.
Closing thoughts
For early-season skiers, Zermatt’s return is welcome news. It brings the Matterhorn’s high slopes back into play just weeks before the main winter opening. The three-month closure also shows how fragile even the Alps’ most reliable snow can be after a hot summer. Hotter summers and thin winter snowpacks leave less snow to protect glacier ice. Anyone planning a trip should check the live lift status before travelling, as conditions and terrain may change at short notice.

full_text:
Seven in ten cultural organisations are concerned about the wellbeing of their staff, freelancers and volunteers working during heatwaves, according to new research from Arts Council England (ACE).
The survey of 296 creative organisations also found that less than 1% felt “very prepared” for extreme heat in the future.
ACE launched the survey after the Met Office provisionally said that this summer was the UK’s hottest on record, with an average mean temperature of 16.5°C, with the highest temperature measured as 38.2°C.
In June, there were multiple full or partial closures of cultural venues due to the heat, including the V&A, the Natural History Museum and the Young V&A museum, with the National Trust shortening the opening hours of several of its properties.
Meanwhile the chief executive of charity Libraries Connected, Isobel Hunter, warned in July that libraries across the UK are “not equipped” to meet the public’s need for respite from high temperatures outside.
ACE said the findings of its survey suggest an “urgent need to strengthen long term resilience and preparedness” in relation to extreme heat conditions, despite many organisations already taking action in response to the heatwaves.
The vast majority (96%) of respondents reported being affected by this year’s heatwaves, with just under half (47%) highlighting “significant or severe” impacts.
Effect on staff
Staff wellbeing was the most reported impact, flagged by 70% of respondents.
Other key issues included reduced attendance at work, untenable indoor working conditions, reduced income for organisations, increased operating costs and cancelled events.
Eight in ten respondents felt that this year’s heatwaves had a worse impact than those in 2025.
According to ACE, many of the organisations surveyed felt that it was too early to calculate accurate financial losses, but the majority believed the heat had a negative impact fiscally.
Of those able to estimate the financial impact, more than three quarters (77%) estimated a loss and 10% forecasted that their losses would end up being more than £10,000.
The highest indoor working space temperature reported was 48°C, with 20 respondents reporting temperatures above 40°C.
Staff at the V&A recently went on strike over issues including heat, with demands including that the institution agrees to close public spaces when temperatures reach 30°C.
Nicola Saunders, ACE’s director of environmental responsibility and innovation, said: “We sincerely thank the creative and cultural sector for its committed response to this survey.
“These insights are incredibly important and essential to inform our work and make sure we are supporting the sector to be resilient as the challenges of extreme weather and other climate change impacts, escalate.”

MUMBAI: The city was under a heatwave warning for the third consecutive day on Wednesday with a yellow alert issued by the IMD.
For October 14, the weather bureau has warned of hot and humid weather conditions in isolated areas as temperatures continue to remain elevated.
Maximum temperatures recorded on Wednesday by the IMD Santacruz observatory was 37.8 degree Celsius which was 4.1 degree Celsius above normal while the IMD Colaba observatory recorded 36.4 degree Celsius which was 3.2 degree Celsius above normal.
Mumbai has been place under a heatwave warning for October 15, with October 16 forecasted to witness hot and humid weather conditions.
Meanwhile light to moderate rain and thundershowers are expected for October 17-18 for Mumbai and Thane.
Just a day ago the city had recorded a maximum temperature of 38 degree Celsius, making it the second-hottest October day in 11 years.
Meanwhile mercury had touched 38.2 degree Celsius on Monday, the highest October maximum recorded in the city during the same period.
IMD officials too agreed that the a prolonged heatwave for early in the month of October wasn’t very common.
“The anticyclone which lead to the first heatwave warning on October 9 last week has shifted slightly northwards, but an easterly wave is influencing the region, with temperatures likely to touch 37.8 degree Celsius on Thursday.
This will mean seven consecutive days of temperatures above 37 degree Celsius, which is unusually oppressive for Mumbai," said an IMD official.
The official further informed, "While the city does experience spells of two to three days of high temperatures, a continuous stretch of six to seven days is not normal. An easterly wave is a weather system characterised by a trough that travels from east to west. It is a feature of this season and can interact with weather systems approaching from the west, triggering intense thunderstorms. Its role in prolonging the current hot spell is a factor that needs to be examined, particularly in the context of a strong El Niño year."
According to Akshay Sunil, vice president, WeatherEx Pvt Ltd, “The heat over Mumbai is part of a broader warm spell across western India. A high-pressure circulation and easterly to northeasterly winds are limiting the usual cooling sea breeze, while clear post-monsoon skies are allowing strong daytime heating. Humidity adds to the discomfort."
"Our extended outlook suggests that above-normal temperatures may continue through at least October 22, although local light showers could bring temporary relief post October 22 in parts of Konkan,” Akshay Sunil added.
